issues.t: Frame rusts through
issues.sym: Clunks or rattles from underneath, rust flakes falling off, holes in the frame or wheel wells, the vehicle swerving, or a failed state safety inspection.
issues.why: The Rodeo's frame and rear underbody have little rust protection, and in salt-belt states they can rot through even when the body looks fine. Owners report shock mounts and spring mounts breaking off, and in one case a loose shock damaged a brake line.
issues.next: Have the frame inspected every year, especially behind the rear wheels. If a frame rail, mount or bracket is rusted through, park the vehicle until it is repaired, because parts can break loose while driving.

issues.t: Rear suspension link brackets rust off the frame (recall)
issues.sym: Clicking or banging from the rear when braking or going over bumps, the Rodeo pulling or swerving, or the rear axle sitting crooked.
issues.why: Rust can eat away the brackets that hold the rear suspension lower links to the frame until one detaches, which hurts handling. Isuzu recalled about 150,000 vehicles in 2010.
issues.next: Ask about recall 10V436000. If you hear new clunks from the rear, have the brackets inspected right away and don't drive it if one is loose.

issues.t: Rear suspension bracket corrosion (recall)
issues.sym: Swaying, clunks from the rear, or a rear lower link mount that has visibly separated from the frame.
issues.why: Excessive rust near the front mounting bracket of the rear suspension lower link can let it break away from the frame. Covered vehicles are those sold or registered in 22 cold-weather states and D.C.
issues.next: Ask about recall 13V547000. Isuzu treats light rust, adds a reinforcement bracket to damaged ones, and offered to buy back vehicles that are too rusted to fix.

issues.t: V6 burns oil and can fail
issues.sym: You add oil often (some owners report a quart a week), there may be blue smoke, and in bad cases the engine knocks, throws a rod or seizes.
issues.why: The 3.2L V6 in these years is prone to heavy oil consumption. If the oil level is allowed to drop, the bearings starve and the engine fails. One owner reported Isuzu issued a service bulletin for the oil burning.
issues.next: Check the oil every fill-up and keep it full. If oil use keeps rising or the engine starts knocking, get a professional diagnosis before it fails completely.

issues.t: Engine knocking and loss of compression at high mileage
issues.sym: A knocking noise from the engine, rough running, and low power, usually well past 100,000 miles.
issues.why: Worn internal engine parts lead to knocking and low compression. Owners of 1996 and 1997 Rodeos report it near the end of the engine's life.
issues.next: Have a compression test done. If the engine is badly worn, a used engine is often an option instead of a rebuild.

issues.t: Coolant leak on top of the engine
issues.sym: Coolant drips or a sweet smell from the top of the engine, a dropping coolant level, and possible overheating.
issues.why: Owners report coolant leaking from the top of the engine on the 1997 at high mileage. The exact source varies, so it has to be traced.
issues.next: Find the leak with a pressure test before the engine overheats. Keep the coolant topped up until it is fixed.

issues.t: Starter fails and engine won't turn over
issues.sym: You turn the key and hear a click or nothing at all, and the engine doesn't crank.
issues.why: Starter motors on the 1996 wear out at high mileage. A weak battery or bad cables can cause the same thing.
issues.next: Have the battery and cables tested first, then the starter.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slips or shifts roughly
issues.sym: Slipping, jerky or rough shifts, a flashing warning light, refusal to go past 20 mph, or the vehicle stalling.
issues.why: Internal transmission wear is the most common cause. Some owners were told the inhibitor (range) switch was sending the wrong signal.
issues.next: Check the fluid and have the codes read. A bad range switch is a simple fix; slipping usually means a rebuild or replacement.

issues.t: Stalls at stops and is hard to start
issues.sym: The engine stalls at red lights or when pulling away, and can be hard to restart.
issues.why: Owners report stalling that dealers often couldn't reproduce. The cause is often hard to find.
issues.next: Note when it happens and have codes read right after a stall. A shop can then check sensors, idle control and wiring.

issues.t: Timing belt problem can stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine cranks but won't start, or stalls while driving and won't restart.
issues.why: Isuzu ran a campaign (01I002000) on the timing belt in these vehicles because a problem could leave the engine unable to run.
issues.next: Ask whether your VIN was covered by campaign 01I002000. Whatever the answer, replace the timing belt at the interval in your owner's manual.

issues.t: ABS can lengthen stopping distance (recall)
issues.sym: The ABS light may come on, and stops take longer than they should.
issues.why: Isuzu recalled over 160,000 vehicles because of an ABS problem that could extend stopping distance.
issues.next: Ask about recall 02I002000. Have the ABS warning light checked if it comes on.

issues.t: Rear lower link bolt can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the rear axle and poor handling.
issues.why: A bolt could detach and separate the lower link from the rear axle.
issues.next: Ask about recall 00V058000 and have the rear links checked if you hear clunking.

issues.t: Engine harness fault can cut fuel (recall)
issues.sym: The engine won't start, or stalls while driving.
issues.why: A cracked terminal in the engine wiring harness can send a false high-speed signal to the engine computer, which then cuts fuel.
issues.next: Ask about recall 98V170000.

issues.t: Fuel return hose can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A gas smell under the hood or fuel dripping in the engine bay.
issues.why: Some fuel return hoses were made with the wrong outer rubber and can crack from ozone exposure.
issues.next: Don't drive with a fuel smell. Ask about recall 00V298000.

issues.t: Fuel pump can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell near the rear of the vehicle or fuel dripping from the tank area.
issues.why: A fault in the fuel pump can let fuel leak, which could cause a fire.
issues.next: Ask about recall 05V466000 and get any fuel smell checked right away.

issues.t: Throttle position sensor fails
issues.sym: Erratic idle, hesitation, poor shifting or a check engine light.
issues.why: The throttle position sensor tells the engine and transmission how far the gas pedal is pressed. When it wears out, both run poorly. Owners report it around 75,000 miles.
issues.next: Have codes read. Replacing the sensor is usually a quick repair.

issues.t: Reduced power and stalling at highway speed
issues.sym: The check engine and reduced power lights come on, the engine stops responding to the gas pedal, and it may stall.
issues.why: Owners report this at high mileage; one mechanic blamed a failing fuel pump. Low oil and worn engines also add to it.
issues.next: Pull over safely if it happens. Have codes read and the fuel pressure tested.

issues.t: Oil use and leaks on later models
issues.sym: The oil level drops between changes with no obvious leak, or oil drips under the vehicle.
issues.why: Owners of 2004 models report the engine using oil or leaking from a hard-to-find source.
issues.next: Check the oil often and keep it full. Have the engine checked for leaks from the valve covers and seals.

issues.t: Check engine and ABS lights come on
issues.sym: The check engine and ABS lights come on, often together.
issues.why: Owners of 2004 models report both lights coming on. The stored codes show which sensor or circuit is at fault.
issues.next: Have both systems scanned. The ABS may not work while its light is on, so brake gently on slippery roads.

issues.t: Knocking when the engine is cold
issues.sym: A knocking or ticking sound for the first minutes after a cold start that fades as the engine warms.
issues.why: Owners report cold-start knock on 2004 models at fairly low mileage. The cause varies and needs a mechanic to listen to it.
issues.next: Use the oil grade in the owner's manual and keep it full. Have it checked if the noise lasts after warm-up.

issues.t: Blower speed control connector melts
issues.sym: The fan stops working on some or all speeds, and there may be a hot plastic smell.
issues.why: The connector at the fan speed control can overheat and melt.
issues.next: Have the connector and blower resistor replaced. Stop using the fan if you smell melting plastic.
